title: Gym Etiquette NZ
meta_desc: Learn unwritten gym rules in NZ to make the most of your workout and respect fellow gym-goers, covering weight racks, machines, and personal space.
intro: As a gym-goer in New Zealand, it's essential to be mindful of the unwritten rules that govern gym etiquette. By following these simple guidelines, you can ensure a positive and respectful experience for both yourself and those around you. In this guide, we'll cover the key aspects of gym etiquette in NZ, from rack-ing your weights to respecting personal space.

sections.heading: Rack Your Weights
sections.body: One of the most fundamental rules of gym etiquette in NZ is to rack your weights after use. This applies to all types of weights, including dumbbells, barbells, and kettlebells. By putting your weights back in their designated place, you help maintain a safe and clutter-free environment for others. Most NZ gym chains, such as City Fitness and Les Mills, have clear signage reminding members to rack their weights.
list: Always return weights to their original place
Don't leave weights on the floor

sections.heading: Wipe Down Machines
sections.body: Another crucial aspect of gym etiquette in NZ is to wipe down machines after use. This helps prevent the spread of germs and keeps the equipment clean for the next user. Many NZ gyms, including Jetts and Anytime Fitness, provide disinfectant wipes and encourage members to use them. By taking a few seconds to wipe down the machine, you can help maintain a hygienic environment and show respect for your fellow gym-goers.
list: Use disinfectant wipes provided by the gym
Wipe down all surfaces that you've come into contact with

sections.heading: Headphones and Personal Space
sections.body: When it comes to headphones and personal space, it's essential to be mindful of those around you. Avoid wearing headphones that may be too loud or distracting, and respect other gym-goers' personal space. This is particularly important during peak hours when the gym can be busy. By being considerate of others, you can help create a positive and respectful atmosphere in the gym.
list: Keep the volume of your headphones at a reasonable level
Be aware of your surroundings and respect others' space
Avoid distractions, such as using your phone, while working out

sections.heading: Peak Hour Tips
sections.body: Peak hours can be challenging, especially in popular NZ gyms like Les Mills and City Fitness. To make the most of your workout during this time, consider the following tips: arrive early to secure your spot, be prepared to share equipment, and be patient with others. By being flexible and considerate, you can minimize wait times and maximize your workout.
list: Arrive early to secure your spot
Be prepared to share equipment or work in with others
Keep your workout concise and efficient

sections.heading: Specific NZ Gym Cultures
sections.body: Different NZ gym chains have unique cultures and expectations. For example, some gyms may have a more social atmosphere, while others may be more focused on individual training. By being aware of these cultural differences, you can adapt your behavior and make the most of your workout. Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme is also available at many NZ gyms, offering discounts of 40-70% off membership prices.
list: Research the gym's culture and expectations before joining
Be open to trying new things and adapting to the gym's environment
Take advantage of Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme
